claim: Export deep-copies the model to CPU eval, strictly captures with torch.export, rejects mutations/randomness, compares eager/captured outputs and exports ONNX.
Input profiles require positive static dimensions and supported dtypes; per-target precision checks reject unsupported combinations.
Public exporter flattens tensor leaves and frozen scalar arguments, validates dense finite inputs and rejects shared input storage.
Audited IREE 3.11.0 imports ONNX and compiles to HAL; static exporter produces package records, not a TorchInductor route.
Static HAL evaluator resolves host orchestration with bounded recursion and operation count and produces dense typed ports.
Only enumerated HAL host operations are accepted; fill/copy/dispatch recipes are recorded and unknown host operations fail.
Package allocator initializes mutable arenas and extracts PTX, actual target, launch metadata, conservative accesses and packed kernel ABI.
Exporter validates closed PTX, target, unresolved external symbols, packed ABI, commands and dense tensor ports.
Stable dtype widths and IDs, public export dtype list and architecture admission thresholds are explicit export policy.
Offline comparison decodes raw BF16/FP8 storage according to declared numeric encoding.
Current audited target list starts at SM60; newer target profiles are explicit conservative SIMT profiles rather than relabeled old targets.
Public export freezes scalar config, performs no implicit precision conversion, stages per-target packages and optionally verifies on a local CUDA device.
Export test accepts keyword-only tensor bias plus frozen strength scalar and verifies typed ports and affine reference outputs.
Tests reject tensor-dependent Python branches, implicit mutation and randomness before compiler calls while preserving inputs/state.
Public package types expose tensor roles/layout/backing size, named bindings and invocation views; package code is trusted executable content.
Runtime validates buffer capacities, tensor layouts, immutable constants, dispatch argument ranges, launch dimensions and copy/fill semantics.
Reader checks version and complete archive, supports PTX/cubin transport, validates before definition registration and retains immutable definitions.
Invoke validates exact tensor interfaces and backing extents, rejects overlap, requires inputs and allocates omitted storage/constants.
Recipe commands expand into retained CUDA dispatch/fill/copy definitions with explicit adjacent ordering, then return ordinary graph tensor views.
Binding fixtures test 64-byte backing extent for Float32[4], reject insufficient/overlapping allocations and preserve permitted aliases.
